reason: Machine lens: TAX, CPX #imm, BCS/BCC and BRA are all real on the 65SC12 (BRA 65C02, 3 cycles, section is cmos). Bytes recounted: old 59 (9+7+30+2+8+3), new 59 (10+7+26+2+4+8+2), so nothing moves and .compiled stays at &9E8A; the whole window sits in page &9E (listing &9E4E-&9E89), so no taken branch or (zp),Y crosses a page before or after. Ranges: BRA columns is -112 (from &9E8A to &9E1A), BCS cell about -50, BCS last_cell forward short: all in range. Semantics: rows_m1 is stored exactly as before at every point; X = rows_m1 on every route into g0a9b_a_test (TAX in the continuing cell, the byte loop leaves X alone; LDX on the carry route and the BCS last_cell route). From last_cell, rows_m1 <= Y <= 7 so CPX #8 falls through (C=0, harmless: .columns re-sets C by CMP and part_byte's DEX/BPL ignore C); from the next cell with Y=7, rows_m1 >= 8 <=> old's 7-rows_m1 borrows, so BCS cell gives the old continuation and the cell test re-runs with SEC. AND #&3F is redundant: s_ptr+1 is &40-&7F on entry (record byte 10 written only at render.6502 1743 from up_in_ring's wrapped value; compiled and kind-cache records have byte 8 >= &80 and branch to .compiled), so SBC gives &3D-&7D and ORA #&40 alone maps it as AND+ORA did; carry unaffected. No self-modified operands in the window; the new label is unique. Cycles recounted per path (not uniform, the claim's 6 is a mix): a column ending in its first cell +4 (CPX+BCS not taken; BRA = JMP at 3); each middle cell of a 3+-cell column +5 (CPX + BCS taken before the old test; TAX +2 cancels AND -2); the final cell of a 2+-cell column -9 (BCC 3 + CPX 2 + BCS 2 vs BCC 3 + TYA/SEC/SBC/BCS 10 + LDX 3); the rare INC route the same. Net per pass = 4*n1 - 9*m + 5*middle; with the window's counts (7.25 columns, 7.05 continuing cells) and the bench's measured -34 a pass this is consistent (m about 5.5) and a saving. Not refuted; the per-execution saving on the hot path is 9 cycles, offset by the slower minority paths.
